item.text: {"text":"BERT4Rec’s random interior-mask task uses right context unavailable during appended-mask next-item inference; therefore, masked-position accuracy alone does not establish next-item quality. The original paper already includes last-item-only masking to reduce this mismatch and examines positional/component ablations. Its evidence supports testing masking ratios and terminal-mask supervision, but does not establish that reconstruction diagnostics predict deployment rankings. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690). Recent work also identifies loss and sampling as confounders: the 2024 gSASRec study links sampled BCE to overconfidence and training instability; this motivates checking optimization before attributing failures to bidirectional attention, without changing the required BERT4Rec family. [Study](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939).\n\nRecommended diagnostic design, rather than an established finding: select targets exclusively within training histories; compare interior reconstruction against prefix-only appended-mask prediction for matched targets, retaining identical candidate sets. Stratify paired rank/HR differences by prefix length, training-item frequency, and elapsed time since the preceding interaction; bootstrap users, keeping each user’s probes together. Report target-rank correlation, top-10 overlap, and cutoff margins alongside uncertainty. Probe sensitivity by removing positional signals, shuffling history, and restricting recent versus distant attention; treat inference perturbations as sensitivity evidence, with controlled retraining needed for stronger architectural claims. Keep the target absent from bidirectional input and read the final nonpadding mask position. Sampling research warns that sampled rankings can misrepresent full-catalog rankings, so keep diagnostic candidate draws fixed and report any full-catalog training-prefix checks separately. [Rank-estimation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371). These probes remain separate from unchanged host macro validation HR@10; they neither justify altering its 99 negatives nor demonstrate improvement without measurement."}
